title: Rhythm & time signatures
examples: What is the difference between 2/4 and 4/4?
How do I know how many beats are in a measure?
Can you show me a rhythm using different note values?

explain.say: Today we are learning about rhythm and time signatures.
First we look at note values like whole, half, and quarter notes.
Next we learn about time signatures like two over four.
A common time signature is four over four, which means four beats.
Three over four means three beats in each measure, like a waltz.
A six over eight signature has six eighth notes in a measure.

items: 1 | 6 | Eighth, Eighth, Eighth, Eighth, Eighth, Eighth

faq.q: What does the top number in a time signature tell me?
faq.a: The top number tells you how many beats are in each measure. You count these beats when you play the music.
asks: How many beats are in a measure?
What does the top number mean?

faq.q: What does the bottom number tell me about the beat?
faq.a: The bottom number tells you which type of note gets one beat. For example, a four means a quarter note gets the beat.
asks: Does the bottom number mean the note type?

faq.q: Is 4/4 the same as common time?
faq.a: Yes, four over four is the same as common time. It means four beats per measure.
asks: Can you name another common time signature?

faq.q: How do I know when to switch between time signatures?
faq.a: The conductor or the music will show you when the time signature changes. You just need to listen carefully.
asks: Do I need to count when the time changes?
How do I follow a change in time?

faq.q: What is the difference between a beat and a measure?
faq.a: A beat is the regular pulse of the music. A measure is a group of beats separated by a bar line.
asks: Are beats and measures the same thing?

facts: A whole note receives four beats in common time.
In 3/4 time, the beat is usually counted as one, two, and three.
The time signature tells you the pattern of beats for a section.
A quarter note usually receives one beat.

quiz.say: If a time signature is 2/4, how many beats are in the measure?
quiz.why: The top number, two, tells you that there are two beats in every measure.

wrong.1: You might think of 4/4 as the most common, so you chose four.
wrong.2: You might mistake the fraction for the answer itself.
wrong.3: You might only look at the bottom number and think of one beat.

quiz.say: If you see a rhythm that fits four quarter notes, what is the most likely time signature?
quiz.why: Since you have four quarter notes, and each gets one beat, the time signature must be four over four.

wrong.0: You might remember the waltz rhythm and pick three.
wrong.1: You might only count the first two notes and stop there.
wrong.2: You might think that because there are many notes, it must be six over eight.
